writes.title: What the mod manager changes
writes.inPlace: A config is a list of console variables (convars), and sometimes engine settings, written into your gameinfo.gi. The mod manager edits the file in place, next to your mods, instead of replacing it.
writes.turnOff: It marks every line it adds or changes, so Turn off removes them and puts back the values they replaced. Your configs and tweaks stay saved.
writes.reapply: A game update or Reset to Vanilla replaces gameinfo.gi. The mod manager writes your config back when it starts, when you switch back to its window, and before every launch from it (vanilla launches included), waiting while Deadlock is running. If you start Deadlock from Steam with the mod manager closed, the config is missing until you open it again.
writes.untouched: SearchPaths, which keeps your mods loading, and video.txt are never changed.

statuses.title: What happens to each setting
statuses.description: Config details, the import review and the settings editor label every line of a config with one of these. Only lines marked Applies are written.
statuses.unchanged: Your gameinfo.gi already has this value, or doesn't set it and the value is the convar's built-in default. Nothing is written.
statuses.blocked: Valve flags this convar as one gameinfo.gi can't set (gameinfo_cannot_override).
statuses.removed: Not in Deadlock's convar list. When the convar history shows it disappearing, the build is named.
statuses.notConvar: Valve lists it as a console command, not a convar.
statuses.engineSection: Outside the ConVars block, such as SceneSystem or RenderSystem. Left out because engine-section edits are off for this config. Deadlock's matchmaking error lists Engine2, MaterialSystem2, NetworkSystem, Particles, RenderSystem, SceneSystem and WorldRenderer as sections where it doesn't support some changes.
statuses.excluded: FileSystem (which holds SearchPaths) and editor-only sections. The mod manager never writes them.
statuses.denied: Keys the mod manager won't write, such as sv_cheats. Each one shows its reason.
statuses.unsupported: The edit doesn't fit your file, for example a section your gameinfo.gi doesn't have.
statuses.camera: Settings that change what you see rather than how fast the game draws it, like field of view or outlines. They're written as the author set them, and you can turn each one off.

scale.title: Categories, the scale and tiers
scale.categories: Valve doesn't group convars, so the mod manager sorts each one into a category by its name: names with "shadow" go to Shadows, for example. A setting can occasionally land in the wrong group.
scale.position: A config's place on the Lighter cuts to Heavier cuts scale comes from how many settings it changes in each category. Shadows count the most; Network and Camera & visibility don't count. It ranks configs against each other and isn't a frame-rate estimate: how many frames a cut gains depends on your hardware.
scale.tiers: Tiers, from Pretty to Potato, are picked by hand for curated and GameBanana configs. Your own configs take the tier of the config they came from.

consent.title: Enable match data sharing?
consent.body:
This signs in to Steam as you in the background, using the login already saved on this PC, to fetch your own Deadlock matches.

• We never see, ask for, or handle your Steam password.
• The saved login stays in memory and only goes to Steam to sign you in. It is never stored, logged, or sent to us or deadlock-api.
• It only asks Steam for your match history. It never touches your inventory, items, trades, Market listings, wallet, or purchases.
• Only match IDs and salts are sent to deadlock-api.
• Fetching is capped at 40 requests per 24 hours.

Because it acts through your real Steam account, the risk is low but not zero.

experimentalTour.title: Want to try something new?
experimentalTour.description: Take a quick look at custom maps.
experimentalTour.duration: The tour takes about a minute. You decide which features to enable.
experimentalTour.pending: Nothing changes until you finish the tour.
experimentalTour.warning: These features are still in development and may have bugs. You can turn them off in Settings → Experimental.
experimentalTour.completeDescription: Open a feature below, or find it later in the sidebar.
experimentalTour.emptyDescription: You can take the tour again from Settings → Experimental.

custom-maps.title: Try a community map
custom-maps.description: Browse maps made by other players.
custom-maps.previewDetail: See what the community has been building.

serverBrowser.title: Play on community servers
serverBrowser.body: Server Browser lists community servers with custom modes and maps. DMM downloads whatever a server needs before you join.

importFromManager.title: Bring your mods over
importFromManager.body: Another mod manager is set up on this PC. Import its mods here instead of downloading them all again.

myModsMenu.title: There's more in this menu
myModsMenu.body: Change the load order, turn every mod on or off at once, export your library, or copy your mod list to share it.

modContextMenu.title: Right-click any mod
modContextMenu.body: Right-click a mod to copy its link, show its files in the game folder, or reinstall it.

loadOrder.title: Choose which mod wins
loadOrder.body: Some of your mods change the same files. Drag them into the order you want to decide which one takes priority.

findBrokenMod.title: Not sure which mod broke the game?
findBrokenMod.body: Use Find a broken mod in this menu. It turns your mods off in halves and narrows down the culprit in a few launches, then puts everything back.

modRepairs.title: Mods acting up after a patch?
modRepairs.body: Use Check mods for repairs in this menu to scan every installed mod against the current game version and see what can be fixed.

modsFolderShortcut.title: Open this folder faster
modsFolderShortcut.body: Press this shortcut anywhere in the app to open the active profile's mods folder.

profiles.title: Keep separate mod setups
profiles.body: Profiles save different sets of mods so you can switch between them without enabling and disabling mods one by one.

remoteInstall.title: Install mods from your phone
remoteInstall.body: Link your GameBanana account and any mod you queue with Remote Install downloads and installs here, even while you're away.

settingsSearch.title: Search every setting
settingsSearch.body: Press this shortcut on the settings page to jump straight to the setting you need.

skinRandomizer.title: Mix up your skins
skinRandomizer.body: Turn on the skin randomizer and each launch picks one of the skins you selected for this hero.

statsCustomize.title: Make this dashboard yours
statsCustomize.body: Add, remove, resize, and rearrange widgets, or create new tabs from templates.

nightlyChannel.title: Like living on the edge?
nightlyChannel.body: Switch to the nightly update channel to get new features before everyone else. Expect the occasional rough edge.
